content.content:
## Budget

- The trees' cost is negligible: on the benchmark, at the game's minimum-spec GPU, 1080p and medium quality, trees add at most 1.0 ms to the average GPU frame time and at most 1.0 ms to the 1% low, compared with the same path with no trees.
- Level selection and fade updates take at most 0.1 ms of main-thread CPU time per frame.
- Players never wait for tree generation: with the shipped cache, trees add at most 0.5 s to a stage's load time compared with the same stage with no trees.
- A run over budget is a failing result in the benchmark's output file.

## Mitigations

- Foliage overdraw. Leaf cards are cut to a tight polygon of 6 to 8 vertices around the opaque part of the leaf texture instead of a full quad, so few pixels are spent on texels that fail the alpha test. Alpha-tested foliage at LOD0 and LOD1 draws in a depth-only pass first and is then shaded only where its depth is equal, so each covered pixel is shaded once.
- Culling. Each frame, instances are culled against the view frustum and against a hierarchical depth buffer built from the previous frame's terrain and trees, on the GPU, and the survivors are compacted into indirect draws. A tree hidden behind a hill or a closer stand of trees costs neither vertices nor pixels.
- Draw calls. Every LOD3 impostor of every species shares one texture array and draws in a single instanced call.
- Foliage shading. Leaf translucency is a cheap wrap-lighting term with a thickness value baked per vertex, not a ray march or extra light lookup; ambient occlusion stays baked. No foliage shader samples more than three textures.
- Geometry. LOD0 of a variant has at most 12,000 triangles for a conifer or broadleaf and 4,000 for a shrub, with branches below a species radius left as plain cards inside the foliage instead of tubes.
- Fades. At most 32 trees fade at once; a tree whose level changes while that many are fading switches at its next free slot, still with a full fade.
- Shadows. Tree shadow casting follows [Lod.shadows](./Lod.md#shadows).
- Load. The cache is generated when the game is built and shipped with it ([Placement.caching](./Placement.md#caching)).

## Hotspots

- Alpha-tested foliage overdraw near the camera, made larger by the 120 m full-detail distance.
- The two levels drawn together during a fade.
- Shadow casters, drawn again for each cascade.
- Stage load on a cold cache, when every variant and impostor is generated.
## Shadows

- Shadows use one level coarser than the one drawn, and never the impostor within the near shadow cascade.
- Only the nearest shadow cascade draws trees with wind and full foliage. Farther cascades draw trees as LOD2 or the impostor with no wind, and re-render their tree casters every fourth frame, the cascades staggered so no two re-render on the same frame.
- Shadow casters are culled per cascade, on the GPU, like the main pass.
- Shadow casters are never dithered. A tree's shadow level switches once, when its fade finishes, so its shadow does not flicker while the tree fades.

## Budget
## Caching

- Generated variants are cached on disk keyed by the species hash, the variant seed and the generator version, and are regenerated whenever any of them changes.
- The game's build generates every variant and impostor of every shipped species and ships the cache, so a player's stage load only reads it. Generation at load only happens for a species or generator changed since the build, as in development or a mod.

- Whole-map meshes are merged per tile, never per object. Many materials = many draws: use a texture array
  (`engine/texture-array.ts` `layeredMaterial`; mesh buildings = one mesh per 192 m tile, start-row lots = 3 material groups
  per 128 m tile). A custom shader must scale `envMapIntensity` (it carries `scene.environmentIntensity`), never replace it.
- Scatter view culling (`InstanceStreamer.setView`, called every frame by the game): non-shadow buckets (LOD1+) are
  angle-sorted and only the camera's view (+ 25 deg) is drawn. LOD0 shadow casters are drawn whole.
- Trees (`trees/`, L-system species in `trees/species.ts`; map rules keep the old tree type ids): 8 variants per species,
  four levels (LOD0-2 geometry + octahedral impostor), switched at 6 % / 2.5 % / 1 % of the screen height (~215 / 520 /
  1300 m for a 15 m tree) and always LOD0 within 120 m. `trees/draw.ts` re-selects every tree near a threshold each
  frame from the camera before shake (`CameraRig.steady`), with a 15 % hysteresis margin and a fixed 0.3 s dithered
  fade per tree; trees settled on a level sit in static batches. LOD1 / LOD2 leaf cards tile the same leaves at the
  LOD0 texel density.
- Tree cost (`trees/stats.ts`): `F6` (= the LOD debug view) shows the tree stats overlay (`trees/overlay.ts`): trees per
  level / fading, draw calls, triangles and GPU ms (timer queries) of the tree main and shadow passes, selection CPU ms,

  dithered. LOD debug view: `?treedebug=1` / `__rally.trees.debug = true` / map viewer checkbox (green LOD0, yellow
  LOD1, orange LOD2, blue impostor, magenta-white = fading, flashing red = more than 2 level changes in 1 s).

  group is distance-culled by `world/distance-cull.ts`. Far scatter chunks of short-range assets are skipped wholesale.

I couldn't make it negligible. After the changes the trees still add about 8–17 ms per frame at 1080p medium on this Radeon 890M, against the spec's 1 ms budget. That's roughly half of what they cost before, measured at a higher resolution than the earlier runs.

The spec step again said `src/` was empty. It isn't, so I changed the existing tree code.

**Benchmark results** (warm cache):

| | Petralica | The Jackie | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| Added average frame time | +8 to +15 ms | +14 to +17 ms | 1.0 ms |
| Added 1% low (99th percentile frame) | +21 to +52 ms | +32 to +45 ms | 1.0 ms |
| Selection and fades, main-thread CPU | 0.5–1.0 ms | 0.65–1.1 ms | 0.1 ms |
| Tree load, warm cache / first visit | ~0.4 s / ~0.55 s | ~0.24–0.43 s / ~0.6 s | 0.5 s |

The ranges are spread across runs: this integrated GPU's clocks vary a lot between runs. Previously it was +18 ms (Petralica) and +31 ms (The Jackie) at 720p. Only the warm-cache load meets its budget, so every run is recorded as a failing result.

**What I implemented from the spec's list:**
- Leaf cards are cut to an 8-vertex outline fitted to the opaque part of the leaf texture.
- Full-detail and first-level foliage draws depth first, then shades each pixel once. On this GPU that makes almost no difference (about 0.5 ms either way), because it's limited by vertex work, not pixel shading.
- All impostors of all species draw in one call from one texture array.
- Leaf shaders read at most 3 textures. Light through leaves is a cheap term using a thickness baked into each vertex. I dropped the image-based lighting from leaves and boost the ambient light to make up for it.
- Full-detail triangle caps hold for every variant: conifers about 10.3k, broadleaves 11.4k, shrubs 2.9k. To fit, thin branches are now flat cards inside the foliage. Conifers also lost the needle clusters on their main limbs, and both large species have fewer, bigger leaf cards per cluster, so they look a little different.
- At most 32 trees fade at once.
- The benchmark checks the budget and writes pass/fail and the reasons into its results file. It now times frames with the GPU timer off, because the timer itself caused the 0.4–1.6 s spikes in last turn's numbers. Tree GPU time comes from a separate pass.

**Spec items not done:**
- **GPU culling against last frame's depth, compacted into indirect draws:** WebGL2 has no compute shaders and no indirect draws. It would need three.js's WebGPU renderer. Culling stays on the CPU, by horizontal view angle only. This is the mitigation that would matter most, since most of the roughly 8,000 geometry trees drawn on The Jackie are hidden behind nearer ones.
- **Rules for farther shadow cascades:** the game has a single shadow map. Its trees already cast with wind and full foliage; farther away there are only baked canopy shadows. So the every-fourth-frame and per-cascade culling rules have nothing to apply to.
- **Generating and shipping the tree cache with the build:** it would add about 65 MB to every download of a web game. The warm browser cache already meets the 0.5 s load budget, and a first visit takes about 0.6 s.
- **0.1 ms of selection CPU:** 2,000–3,000 trees still need re-checking every frame because the detail thresholds sit so far out. Getting under 0.1 ms on the main thread would mean moving selection into a worker. I didn't do that.

Hitting 1 ms needs a choice: GPU culling (WebGPU), or bringing the detail thresholds back closer. Last time you asked for full detail out to 120 m and LOD changes out to about 1.3 km, and that is now what keeps the cost high.

Tests (502), lint and the type check pass, and `DETAILS.md` is updated. Nothing is committed.

```suspense-question
The trees still cost about 8–17 ms per frame on this GPU, against the 1 ms budget, mostly because thousands of trees are drawn in full or near-full detail out to over a kilometre. What should give?
- Bring the detail thresholds back closer (for example full detail within 60 m), trading some close-up detail for speed
- Move the trees to three.js's WebGPU renderer so the GPU can cull hidden trees, keeping the far detail distances
- Relax the budget to what this approach can reach (around 5 ms per frame)
```
